question: What will be the winning margin in Brazil’s 2026 presidential election runoff?

calls.reasoning: First round: Flávio 47.03 vs Lula 45.16 (lead 1.87). The other candidates took 7.58%, mostly right-leaning (Caiado and Zema endorsed Flávio; Renan Santos and Cury neutral). A 60-65% transfer to Flávio implies a ~3.4-4.2pt margin. The PoderData poll (Oct 5-7) has Flávio 53-47 in valid votes. Polymarket and Kalshi give Flávio 84% to win. Polymarket's thin runoff-margin market prices Flávio by 4-8 at 49.5%, Flávio by under 4 at 33.5%, and Lula by under 4 at 13%. A reported Datafolha Lula 48-43 result is unverified. The question scores the absolute margin, so a Lula win also produces a small value. Historical shifts between rounds and the first-round polling error justify wide dispersion; I put 10% on a margin above 8.
calls.dossier:
- First round Oct 4 2026 (TSE via Exame/Terra): Flávio Bolsonaro 47.03% valid, Lula 45.16%; gap ~2.2M votes. Flávio won 4 of 5 regions; Lula won only the Northeast.
- Other candidates totaled 7.58% of valid votes (Terra/ric.com.br, Oct 5-6). Caiado (5th, 2.18%) and Zema endorsed Flávio. Renan Santos (Missão) and Augusto Cury (Avante) are neutral; Santos said Flávio is 'already elected'.
- Turnout ~72%, 33.4M abstentions (Al Jazeera, Oct 6). Turnout changes in the runoff can shift the margin.
- Flávio beat the final first-round polls by ~3pts (Datafolha Oct 3 had Lula 45 vs Flávio 42 in valid votes). Al Jazeera credits early strategic consolidation on the right, the Banco Master scandal, and economic frustration.
- PoderData/Aya (phone, n=3000, Oct 5-7, pub Oct 8, CNN Brasil): Flávio 53% vs Lula 47% valid votes in the runoff.
- Datafolha (n=2520, in person, Oct 6-8, pub Oct 8): a search snippet claimed Lula 48 vs Flávio 43 total, but the source pages I opened did not contain runoff numbers. Unverified.
- Quaest first runoff poll scheduled ~Oct 12; AtlasIntel ~Oct 9.
- Pre-first-round Datafolha runoff simulations: Lula 46-44 (Sep 17), 47-45 (later).
- Historical runoff margins: 2002 ~22.6, 2006 ~21.2, 2010 ~12.1, 2014 3.3 (first-round lead 8.0), 2018 10.3 (first-round lead 16.7), 2022 1.8 (first-round lead 5.2). The first-round leader won every runoff 2002-2022.
- Resolves off the TSE final nationwide valid-vote shares (excluding blank/null), as the absolute winner-minus-runner-up gap; NOT total-vote poll figures.
- Event window: runoff vote Oct 25 2026 -> TSE result; as of Oct 8, 2026, the campaign between rounds (Oct 4 -> Oct 25) is ~19% elapsed of 21 days... (4 of 21 days).
- Searched, not found: verified Datafolha runoff numbers; AtlasIntel runoff poll; Kalshi margin market.
calls.reference_class: Brazilian presidential runoffs 2002-2022: change from first-round lead between the top two to final runoff margin, plus allocation of eliminated candidates' votes

calls.reasoning: First round: Flavio 47.03 vs Lula 45.16; Caiado (2.18) and Zema endorsed Flavio, Cury and Santos neutral, so simple transfers imply Flavio ~52-53 (margin ~5). Datafolha Oct 6-8 has Lula 48-43, but its first-round poll overstated Lula by ~5pts; PoderData has Flavio 53-47 among valid votes. Polymarket and Kalshi winner markets ~84% Flavio; a thin Polymarket margin market centres near Flavio +4. Modeled signed margin N(3.5, 3.5) and took the absolute value; ~10% mass above 8 (a Flavio landslide if poll bias persists).
calls.dossier:
- TSE first round Oct 4 2026 (100% counted): Flavio Bolsonaro (PL) 47.03% (56.10M), Lula (PT) 45.16% (53.88M); Cury 2.89, Renan Santos (Missao) 2.24, Caiado 2.18, Zema 0.27; turnout 78.92% [Wikipedia; Rio Times].
- Endorsements: Caiado and Zema -> Flavio; Hertz Dias (0.04) and Edmilson Costa (0.02) -> Lula; Cury, Santos and Grassi no endorsement [Wikipedia, as of Oct 8].
- An 87-seat congressional bloc voted to endorse Flavio [Rio Times headline, Oct 2026].
- Datafolha Oct 6-8 (n=2520, MoE 2): Lula 48%, Flavio 43% total voting intention [CartaCapital/Folha, Oct 8].
- PoderData/Aya Oct 5-7 (n=3000 phone, MoE 1.8): Flavio 53%, Lula 47% of valid votes [CNN Brasil].
- First-round polling error: Datafolha's final poll (Oct 3) had Lula 45, Flavio 42 of valid votes vs actual Flavio +1.87, a ~5pt miss toward Lula; Quaest final had Lula 46, Flavio 45 [Rio Times; NBC].
- Upcoming polls: AtlasIntel Oct 9 (n=5000 online), Quaest Oct 12 (n=1104) [Brasil de Fato, Oct 6].
- Past runoff margins (pp of valid votes): 2002 23.2, 2006 21.6, 2010 12.1, 2014 3.3, 2018 10.3, 2022 1.8. In 2022 the final polls had Lula ~+5 valid vs actual +1.8.
- Resolves off the TSE final national runoff result: winner share minus runner-up share among valid votes (blank and null excluded); the margin is always >=0 regardless of who wins; the range is 0-8 with an open upper bound.
- Event window: runoff Oct 25 2026, single day; as of Oct 8 the campaign is ~17 days from the vote.
- Searched but not found: Kalshi margin markets, any Cury/Santos endorsement, post-first-round Quaest/AtlasIntel numbers.

calls.reasoning: First round: Flavio 47.03 vs Lula 45.16, with ~7.8% to mostly right-leaning minor candidates (Cury 2.89, Renan Santos 2.24, Caiado 2.18); a 60/40-70/30 transfer to Flavio implies a runoff margin of ~3.4-5pts. Runoff polls are split: Datafolha had Lula +1-3 pre-R1 (but R1 polls underestimated the right by ~5pts), PoderData Oct 5-7 shows Flavio 53-47 valid, AtlasIntel ~tied (Oct 3). Markets: Polymarket ~85% Flavio (main market, $175M); a thin (~$7.5k) Polymarket runoff-margin market priced Flavio by 4-8 at 49.5%, Flavio by under 4 at 33.5%, Lula by under 4 at 13% (bands differ; treated as evidence only). Kalshi had Flavio 82% on Oct 5. Signed margin modeled as N(+3.5, 3.5) and folded; ~9% mass above 8 (a landslide like 2018's 10.3).
calls.dossier:
- First round Oct 4, 2026 (TSE via Exame, Oct 2026): Flavio Bolsonaro (PL) 47.03%, Lula (PT) 45.16%; Augusto Cury 2.89%, Renan Santos (Missao) 2.24%, Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) 2.18%; others small. Flavio won 4 of 5 regions; Lula won only the Northeast.
- Al Jazeera Oct 6: pre-election polls had Lula ~3pts ahead in R1; actual Flavio +1.9 (polling miss ~5pts toward the right), attributed to early strategic consolidation of minor right-wing voters, the Banco Master scandal, and economic frustration. Lula trails by 2.2M votes; ~9M minor-candidate votes and 33M+ abstentions are in play.
- Datafolha pre-R1 simulated runoffs: Sep 24 Lula 47 / Flavio 45; Sep 29-Oct 1 Lula 48 / Flavio 45; Oct 1-3 Lula 47 / Flavio 46 (total votes).
- PoderData/Aya (phone, n=3000, fieldwork Oct 5-7, released Oct 8): valid votes Flavio 53 / Lula 47.
- AtlasIntel (Oct 3): Lula 50.1 / Flavio 49.9 valid votes; first AtlasIntel runoff poll due Oct 9 (n=5000). Datafolha's first runoff poll (fieldwork Oct 6-8, n=2520) was released Oct 8; secondary reports of its numbers conflict (one says Lula 48, Flavio 43), unverified. Quaest's first runoff poll is due Oct 12.
- Historical Brazilian runoff margins (pts of valid votes): 2002 22.8, 2006 21.6, 2010 12.0, 2014 3.3, 2018 10.3, 2022 1.8. In 2022 the R1-to-R2 gain was larger for the right-wing candidate (43.2 to 49.1) than for Lula (48.4 to 50.9).
- Arithmetic: if the ~7.8% minor-candidate vote splits 60/40 to Flavio, the runoff is ~51.7/48.3 (margin 3.4); 70/30 gives ~52.5/47.5 (margin 5.0); 50/50 gives ~51/49 (margin 1.9). Differential turnout could change this.
- Resolves off the TSE final national valid-vote shares (winner minus runner-up, sign-free, absolute margin), not off polls. Range 0-8 with an open upper bound (a margin above 8 is possible, e.g. 2018's 10.3).
- Event window: runoff Oct 25, 2026; as of Oct 8, 17 days remain until the vote.
- Searched but not found: endorsements by Caiado, Cury and Renan Santos for the runoff; the verified Datafolha Oct 8 topline.
calls.reference_class: Brazilian presidential runoffs 2002-2022 (margins 22.8, 21.6, 12.0, 3.3, 10.3, 1.8), adjusted for first-round gap + transfer of minor-candidate vote

calls.reasoning: R1: Flavio 47.03 vs Lula 45.16; ~7.8% minor vote leans right (Caiado, Zema endorsed Flavio), so transfer arithmetic implies Flavio +3.4 to +5. Post-R1 polls conflict: PoderData Flavio 53-47 valid vs a reported Datafolha Lula 48-43 total; Datafolha overstated Lula ~5pts in R1. Winner markets ~84% Flavio. Signed margin modeled ~N(+3.5,3.5), folded since the question uses an absolute margin; ~9% mass above 8 for a landslide if the right's polling miss persists.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agree on the R1 result, endorsements and PoderData; they differ only on judgment and minor facts. The Datafolha Oct 6-8 topline (Lula 48-43) is cited by Run 2 via CartaCapital/Folha but unverified by Runs 1 and 3; I cannot check it without web access, so I give it partial weight, discounted for Datafolha's ~5pt R1 pro-Lula miss, and let it widen the distribution rather than shift it. The turnout discrepancy (72% vs 78.92%) cannot be settled and is immaterial. I carry forward the folded N(+3.5,3.5) reading that the transfer arithmetic, PoderData and winner markets jointly support, with the median ~3.3 and a 9% upper escape.
